sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 490.3 ± 39.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell surface ELISA detecting the HA tag confirmed surface display of the tagged full-length receptor (L6); SP-HA-mGPR83 surface expression comparable to wild-type levels (L5). No ligand-binding or G-protein signaling assay of the tagged construct is reported in the ledger.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the HA tag was cloned downstream of the signal peptide of Gpr83, creating a full-length membrane-anchored construct. The signal peptide spans residues 1–16 (computed landmarks), so the junction is after residue 16 (A) and before residue 17 (T), the mature N-terminus. Python confirms seq[15]='A' and seq[16]='T'. The tag sits 55 residues from TM1 (starts at 72), well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum, in the large extracellular N-terminal domain. L5 and L6 independently confirm surface display by ELISA. Full-length, membrane-anchored GPR83 construct with HA tag cloned downstream of the signal peptide (SP-HA), expressed in COS-7 cells and confirmed at the cell surface by HA-detecting ELISA and immunofluorescence. Multiple independent groups (PMC4300838, PMC3546042, PMC3709495, PMC5148169, PMC10606834) used this identical SP-HA architecture.

sources.claim: A hemagglutinin tag was cloned downstream of the signal peptide of Gpr83 (SP-HA, see Figure 1 B for schematic representation).

literature_notes: All nine ledger lines converge on a single architectural motif: HA tag inserted immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site (SP-HA), which maps to insert_after_residue=16 in UniProt canonical numbering. L2, L3, and L4 also mention an 'NHA' or 'amino-terminal end' construct (tag before residue 1, i.e., insert_after_residue=0); however, a tag placed N-terminal to the signal peptide is co-translationally cleaved with the signal peptide and cannot be displayed on the extracellular surface — this is a silent failure mode, not a surface site, and it is placed in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tag in any extracellular loop (ECL1 131–145, ECL2 207–237, ECL3 314–325) or at the C-terminus. L5 describes a deletion construct (del17–60) that still carries the HA at the SP-HA junction; it does not define a new insertion site. L9 references a previously described HA-tagged mGPR83 plasmid with no positional detail beyond what L1–L4 already establish.

literature_other_positions.note: NHA construct places the HA tag at the amino-terminal end (before residue 1, i.e., upstream of the signal peptide); a tag at this position is co-translationally cleaved with the signal peptide (residues 1–16) and cannot be displayed on the extracellular surface.
